issues.title: Unqualified inclusion of pressure-admissible states in the acoustic set

failure_location.quote: It is clearly that $\mathcal G^p\subset \mathcal G$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal G=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ c^2(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}
\mathcal G^p=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ p(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that every state in the positive-pressure set \(\mathcal G^p\) automatically belongs to the positive-sound-speed set \(\mathcal G\). The old formulas support this only with an additional acoustic sign condition, such as \(p+p_{w,k}>0\) for both phases. For example, under the stated assumptions take \(\gamma_1=\gamma_2=2\), \(p_{w,1}=-1.01\), \(p_{w,2}=0\), \(z_1=0.02\), both partial densities equal to one, zero momentum, and \(E=0.9596\). The mixture formula gives \(p=1>0\), but the Wood reciprocal is \(0.02/[2(1-1.01)]+0.98/[2(1+0)]=-0.51\), so \(c^2<0\). Thus the old paper establishes the inclusion only after an unstated restriction; without it, \(\mathcal G^p\) can contain acoustically inadmissible states.
issues.overall_effect: The old justification for treating \(\mathcal G^p\) as a stricter physical admissible set is invalid for the full stated Tammann parameter class. The convexity theorem for \(\mathcal G^p\) itself remains valid and is not a dependent affected result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional inclusion with the qualified statement that every state U in G^p satisfying p(U)+p_{w,k}>0 for k=1,2 belongs to G; in particular, G^p is contained in G when both reference pressures are nonnegative. Add the one-line justification that ρ_k c_k²=γ_k(p+p_{w,k}) makes Wood's reciprocal positive. The convexity theorem for G^p and the later method need no alteration.
issues.why_classification: The claim omits a genuine acoustic-sign premise and therefore is not a typo. The needed qualification is short, standard, satisfied by the parameter regimes used in the paper, and preserves the intended physical comparison without affecting any dependent result, so the issue is minor.

issues.title: Invalid endpoints in the advertised nonconvexity counterexample

failure_location.quote:
Specifically, for the Kapila five-equation model closed 
by the Tammann EOS, 
we provide a concrete counterexample 
in Appendix A to demonstrate 
that the admissible set $\mathcal{G}$ is non-convex.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that Appendix A provides a concrete counterexample proving that \(\mathcal G\) is nonconvex. The appendix actually uses \(\mathbf U^{(1)}\) with \(z_2\rho_2=0\) and \(\mathbf U^{(2)}\) with \(z_1\rho_1=0\), while the displayed definition requires both quantities to be strictly positive. Consequently, the old appendix supplies no valid pair of endpoints in \(\mathcal G\), although the nonconvexity conclusion itself can be recovered by a nearby interior perturbation.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed explicit proof of nonconvexity is invalid as written. The convexity theorem for \(\mathcal G^p\) and later formal results do not depend on this counterexample.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the appendix endpoints by U_delta^(1)=[1.2,delta,0,1000,1-delta]^T and U_delta^(2)=[delta,1000,0,6001,delta]^T for sufficiently small delta>0. Both endpoints then satisfy the strict partial-density conditions. Continuity and the strict sign margins preserve c²>0 at both endpoints, while their midpoint retains z_1=1/2, zero momentum, E=3500.5, and the strictly negative Wood reciprocal. Thus the same nonconvexity claim follows.
issues.why_classification: The original endpoints genuinely violate the definition, so a mathematical perturbation check is required and the defect is not a typo. The explicit interior perturbation is nevertheless short and routine, recovers the exact nonconvexity conclusion, and affects no later result; hence the issue is minor.

issues.title: Wrong pressure-force sign in the split momentum RHS
issues.failure_explanation: Both the governing equation and its compact flux definition place \(+p\mathbf I\) inside a flux whose divergence is subtracted on the right-hand side. Thus the expanded pressure force must carry a negative sign. The old literal term \(+p\mathbf I\) has the opposite sign. The latest version flips this sign, although it still does not write the required divergence of the pressure tensor.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the old transport substep applies the pressure contribution in the wrong direction. The detailed DG flux elsewhere uses the correct conservative flux, so no later formal result is dependent on this sign typo. The latest fixes the sign component but remains malformed because of the independent missing divergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the pressure contribution in the split momentum right-hand side to have the negative sign dictated by the conservative momentum equation, namely the pressure part of −∇·(ρu²+pI). No DG flux, proof, or downstream result needs modification.
issues.why_classification: The governing equation and compact flux both place +pI inside the left-hand-side flux divergence, uniquely forcing a negative pressure force on the right-hand side. The detailed DG discretization already uses that correct flux, so an intended reader can correct this transcription without repairing any inference or construction.

issues.title: Pressure secant limiter does not enforce the pressure floor
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm claims that its value of \(\theta_p\) enforces \(p\geq\varepsilon_p\). Writing the old pressure as \(p=N/D\), however, gives \(D(z_1)=z_1/(\gamma_1-1)+z_2/(\gamma_2-1)\), which varies along the scaling segment. With zero momentum, \(N\) is affine. For \(\gamma_1=1.4\), \(\gamma_2=4.4\), \(z_A=0.1\), and \(z_B=0.9\), one has \(D_B>D_A\). Choose realizable endpoint energies with \(p_A=1\) and \(p_B=\varepsilon_p/2\). The old ordinary pressure secant chooses \(\theta_p\) so that the unweighted interpolation equals \(\varepsilon_p\), but the exact level-set margin at that point is proportional to \(D_A-D_B<0\). Hence the limited state has \(p<\varepsilon_p\).
issues.overall_effect: The old limiter does not guarantee membership in \(\mathcal G^p\), so its pressure-positivity and pressure-bound-preservation claims fail. Its scalar affine scaling still preserves cell averages and linear identities, so the Abgrall formal results are not defeated by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let N(U) be the displayed pressure numerator and D(U)=z_1/(γ_1−1)+z_2/(γ_2−1). Replace the pressure secant by a secant for g_epsilon(U)=N(U)−epsilon_p D(U)=D(U)(p(U)−epsilon_p): if g_min=min over the quadrature set of g_epsilon evaluated at the Step-1 state is negative, set theta_p=g_epsilon(Ubar)/(g_epsilon(Ubar)−g_min), and otherwise set theta_p=1. The existing kinetic-energy inequality makes N concave, while D is affine, so g_epsilon is concave and the scaled states satisfy p≥epsilon_p. This retains the cell average, the Step-1 linear bounds, and the Abgrall linear identities.
issues.why_classification: The old secant uses a genuinely unsuitable nonlinear pressure value, so the issue is substantive rather than a typo. However, the pressure decomposition and concavity argument already present in the source yield a short, local replacement that restores the same floor, admissible-set guarantee, method, and complexity without weakening any affected claim or changing proof architecture. The issue is therefore minor.
